analytic_proof_obligations: C_n equals marked collision length in distribution
one-dimensional Rayleigh tightness and tail limit
two-dimensional local limit and boundary tightness

model.components: K_n is the number of weak components, equivalently directed cycles
model.cyclic_points: C_n is the number of vertices on directed cycles
model.functional_graph: one directed edge v->f(v) from every labelled vertex
model.marked_orbit: from vertex 1, mu is the tail length, lambda the eventual cycle length, and R=mu+lambda
model.state_space: all functions f:[n]->[n], each with probability n^(-n)

nonclaims: Workspace ownership is not a literature-priority claim.
Ensemble averages are not the orbit zeta or determinant of one deterministic map.
No canonical same-clock operator is inferred from the random ensemble.

proof_contract.decomposition: choose cyclic labels, a permutation with r cycles, then a rooted forest into those labels
proof_contract.finite_evidence_role: exhaustive enumeration is regression evidence and not a proof of the all-n theorem
proof_contract.forest: the all-minors directed matrix-tree determinant is det(nI-J)=k n^(n-k-1)
proof_contract.joint_limit: a two-dimensional local product limit plus tightness gives the stated density
proof_contract.marked_orbit: choose an ordered collision-free prefix and force its closing edge
proof_contract.rayleigh: the no-collision tail product converges after the square-root scaling

sources.author: Bernard Harris
sources.title: Probability Distributions Related to Random Mappings

sources.author: Philippe Flajolet and Andrew M. Odlyzko
sources.title: Random Mapping Statistics

theorem_contract.distribution_identity: C_n and R_n=mu+lambda have the same law
theorem_contract.joint_count: N(n,k,r)=binom(n,k)c(k,r) k n^(n-k-1), with the rooted-forest factor interpreted as 1 at k=n
theorem_contract.joint_limit: (mu,lambda)/sqrt(n) has limiting density exp(-(x+y)^2/2) on x,y>=0
theorem_contract.rayleigh: C_n/sqrt(n) and R_n/sqrt(n) converge to Rayleigh density x exp(-x^2/2)
